name: AutoTrust-JEV-27B-v1.1
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear attention with full gated attention every 4th layer (16 of 64); partial RoPE
notes: ADDED 2026-11-10 from the HF trending feed (trendingScore 118.5, created 2026-10-17, 1,400 likes). A decision model (task=decision): it returns per-option probabilities for a schema of typed questions in ONE forward pass with no generated text, so chat and refusal benchmarks say nothing about it - it is excluded from the worth-running ranking by construction and belongs in docs/33-decision-models.md. Derived from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B: the sibling autotrust/JEV-27B tags base_model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, and this v1.1 has the same 27,356,728,560-parameter tensor set (identical safetensors total). It does NOT carry a base_model tag of its own, which is why base_model was passed explicitly; every architecture field above is inherited unchanged from the base record models/qwen3-8-27b (64 layers, hybrid Gated DeltaNet with full attention every 4th layer = 16 of 64, hidden 5120, 16 query / 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, 262144 native context). PARAMS: 27.357B from safetensors (all BF16); active equals that on the schema's dense basis, and flops_per_token_active = 2 x 27.781e9 = 5.5562e10 using the base record's active count, matching the convention already used by models/clef and models/jev-27b-vl. Note params_b (27.357) is below active_params_b (27.781) for the same reason as arete-27b: the MTP head is not in the released checkpoint. KV inherits 65,536 B/token = 16 full-attention layers x 2 x 4 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 2 B; the 48 linear-attention layers hold a constant DeltaNet state and are excluded. HARDWARE GATE: passes - 27.357B active (<= 40) and 27.357 x 0.5 = 13.7 GiB at the 4-bit planning figure. Card says serve with MAX_LEN=32768 on an 80 GB card. WHAT THE CARD CLAIMS: public index 67.31 on Decision Index 0.3 (37 benchmarks, 140,178 completed scoreable requests, official kit commit f5a6e4f, vLLM 0.31.0, 1x B300, 16 concurrent clients), with area skill scores Tools 85.19 / Language 73.38 / Retrieval 66.97 / Knowledge 55.16 / Arts 51.08. The card also prints a RAW index of 75.62 and warns explicitly that raw and skill index are different metrics - only 67.31 is recorded here. SELF-REPORTED: the card states 'complete local evaluation using the official evaluation kit, self-reported pending maintainer verification', so every row has vendor_claim true, and the card reports no private/Full score. LATENCY is local and concurrent (median 64.8 ms, mean 178.8 ms, p95 800.5 ms, 16 clients on one B300) - the card itself says these are not standardised leaderboard-hardware measurements, so they are quoted in prose and NOT entered as board latency. ECE is not printed for this run and is left null rather than invented. NOT RANKABLE AGAINST THE BOARD: the catalog's decision_index.jsonl and docs/33 carry editions 0.2.1 and 0.4.1. This run is on 0.3, a third scale, so it is deliberately NOT appended to decision_index.jsonl (that file is only updated from an actual board read) and no rank is claimed; 67.31 is not comparable to the 0.4.1 index values. WHAT IT LOSES, per its own tables: on GPQA Diamond 54.59 vs Jev 1.14 at 75.51, MMLU-Pro 73.65 vs 82.13, CLadder 81.02 vs 88.58, HLE 16.57 vs 19.36, MMLU-Pro and BBH fixed-option both trail Jev 1.14; the card calls HLE near chance and ChessBench, humour preference and consensus ranking weak. It does beat both reference columns broadly else where (BFCL 97.23, CLINC150+OOS 97.08, WinoGrande 95.26, CRUXEval 85.44) - but those reference columns are the labs' published runs, not re-runs, so the card's own warning applies: descriptive cross-run comparison. LICENCE apache-2.0, including its decision readout head.
